description: One "my stack" page: a named set of RealUptime-tracked services, each with the SAME plate level its own page shows (down / partially_down / degraded / partially_degraded / blocked / no_data / partially_unverified / up, with label and clause), plus the stack's roll-up: `summary.headline` ("2 of 6 services down or degraded"), the worst member level, and counts by state. Pass `stack`, the stack's slug (from its URL, https://realuptime.io/outages/stack/<slug>) or id. Stacks are built at https://realuptime.io/outages/stack or from a Monitor dashboard; there is no list endpoint, a caller must hold the key. User reports, public chatter and the vendors' own status pages are not read for a stack (those signals are published as null), so `reachable_reports_elevated` never appears here; a member's own page still shows it. An unknown key answers `summary.level: "not_found"`, which says nothing about any service's health. Readings are RealUptime's own probe measurements, never user reports and never the vendor's status page. "blocked" means our probe was refused, which is NOT a confirmed outage. A no-data answer is never a healthy answer. Cite the returned source.url when repeating any of this.
name: get_stack
